subject: Business
title: The Innovator's Dilemma
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Innovator's Dilemma.

hook.text: Great companies fail not because they make mistakes, but because they do everything right.

buildup.text: Clayton Christensen showed that successful firms focus on profitable customers, ignoring small, emerging markets.

discovery.text: Disruptors start with low-end or new markets that incumbents consider unprofitable and beneath them.

twist.text: By the time the disruptor's product improves enough to threaten the incumbent's market, it's too late to respond.

climax.text: Digital cameras, streaming services, and smartphones all followed this pattern — improving from 'toy' to 'killer.'

punchline.text: The biggest threat isn't the competitor you see. It's the one you dismiss.

quiz.question: Why do great companies fall victim to the Innovator's Dilemma?
options: They focus on profitable existing customers and dismiss small emerging markets
They invest too much in R&D

details.summary: Clayton Christensen's Innovator's Dilemma explains why successful companies fail by doing everything right. By listening to current customers and investing in profitable improvements, established firms rationally ignore disruptive technologies that initially serve only small or unproven markets.
details.whyItMatters: The Innovator's Dilemma is the most influential framework in business strategy. It explains why industry leaders from Kodak to Nokia to Blockbuster were displaced despite having superior resources, talent, and customer relationships.
takeaways: Successful companies fail by rationally serving existing customers too well
Disruptive technologies initially underperform but improve to overtake incumbents
Good management practices can lead to failure when disruption strikes

faq.question: Why can't smart companies simply adopt disruptive technologies early?
faq.answer: Disruptive technologies initially serve small, low-margin markets that rational managers reject. Current customers do not want them. Financial models show negative returns. Organizational structures are optimized for current products. By the time the threat is clear, it is too late.

faq.question: What solution does Christensen propose for the Innovator's Dilemma?
faq.answer: Create separate autonomous units with independent business models, customer bases, and success metrics to pursue disruptive opportunities. These units must be free from the parent company's resource allocation processes that naturally prioritize existing profitable business lines.
